answer: Each identity opens only one live session per epoch by posting a signed heartbeat bound to this epoch's seed and a monotone clock. Three established witnesses, drawn by public sortition, record that timestamp and later countersign mining only if later heartbeats arrive at least fifteen minutes apart and never reuse a clock value. A farm still pays one stretched lease per key: it cannot pack a canyon of aliases into the same minute, nor float an ocean of attestations off one clock, and a hollow reused timestamp is rejected on the ledger.
